title: Handover tests
description: tests.json in a frozen handover (handovers/<id>/), written by Core.handoverTests at freeze for every handover that has an element with a code area (d.code), listed and hashed in handover.yaml (named there as `tests:`). It maps tests to elements statically (project references, co-location, imports) from the registry's asbuilt/facts.json; there is no coverage or call-graph data. designc does not know tasks, so it is keyed per element (the ids of elements.json): a consumer maps a task to its tests through the task's elements. facts.json is not copied, so its sha256 is in the handover id (a handover frozen against other facts is a different handover). An element with code and no pass_to_pass entry is listed in `unmapped`: coverage information, never a gate clause. designc owns this contract; consumers conform to it. docs/handover-tests.example.json is the shared fixture.

facts.description: The as-built facts the map was derived from; null when the registry has no asbuilt/facts.json (every coded element is then unmapped).

sha256.description: sha256 of the facts file's bytes, as in the handover id.

elements.description: Only elements with a code area (and, in an item handover, in scope), in elements.json order.

repo.description: The element's d.repo, when split repos are declared.

fail_to_pass.description: Tests that must turn green: the element's generated acceptance specs, and the page test of a screen whose component is this element. Sorted by path.

pass_to_pass.description: Existing tests that must stay green, found statically. Sorted by path.

unmapped.description: Elements with a code area and no pass_to_pass entry.

enum: no existing test references its code

path.description: Repo-relative (in split repos, prefixed with the repo key as extract writes it), or inside the handover for generated specs.

command.description: Run from the repo root; null for a test that is listed and not runnable (node).

via.description: pass_to_pass only: how it was tied to the element.
